stories.headline: SoftBank overtakes Toyota as Japan's most valuable company on AI rally

key_facts.fact: SoftBank shares jumped as much as 13% to a record high of 8,546 yen on Monday, pushing the company's market cap to roughly 47-48 trillion yen ($288-306 billion), ahead of Toyota at about 45.7-46 trillion yen after Toyota fell 4.8-4.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: Softbank surged over 13% to a record high of 8,546.0 yen, and was among the biggest boosts to the Nikkei 225, which added 1%. Monday's gains put Softbank's valuation at a peak of 48 trillion yen, or $305.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank shares are up more than 80% in 2026, while Toyota shares are down more than 10%.
key_facts.excerpt: The surge has propelled SoftBank shares up more than 80% this year, pushing the company's market value above ¥46 trillion ($288 billion), higher than Toyota's roughly ¥45.8 trillion. Toyota shares, by contrast, have fallen more than 10% this year.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank had not surpassed Toyota in market value in more than two decades, since briefly doing so at the peak of Japan's internet bubble in 2000.
key_facts.excerpt: If the gains hold through the close, SoftBank will surpass Toyota in market value for the first time in more than two decades, a feat that it only briefly achieved back at the peak of Japan's internet bubble in 2000.

key_facts.fact: Masayoshi Son told La Tribune Dimanche over the weekend that SoftBank would invest 75 billion euros ($87.5 billion) over five years building AI infrastructure in France, calling it 'the largest investment in Europe in infrastructure related to artificial intelligence'.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank, a major backer of ChatGPT maker OpenAI, soared more than 11 percent in the afternoon trade, after its founder announced a 75-billion-euro ($87.5 billion) investment in AI infrastructure in France. Masayoshi Son told La Tribune Dimanche weekly on Saturday that it 'will be the largest investment in Europe in infrastructure related to artificial intelligence'.

key_facts.fact: Japan's Nikkei 225 topped 67,000 for the first time on Monday; SoftBank alone contributed 618 points of the Nikkei's 709-point rise.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's Nikkei share average topped 67,000 for the first time on Monday, powered by AI-related shares... SoftBank was by far the ‌biggest support for ⁠the index, ⁠jumping 10.3% to contribute 618 points of the Nikkei's total 709-point rise.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank retains roughly 90% ownership of Arm Holdings, whose shares have more than tripled in 2026; its stake and an OpenAI investment gain drove a quadrupling of annual net profit to over $30 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Softbank's latest rally was driven chiefly by optimism over its exposure to chipmaking and AI processors through its ownership of chip designer Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM). Softbank retains roughly 90% ownership of Arm. Shares of the chip designer have more than tripled in value so far in 2026.

stories.headline: China issues sweeping outbound investment rules expanding scrutiny of tech and data deals

key_facts.fact: China's State Council on Monday published Decree No. 837, signed by Premier Li Qiang, formalizing 34 articles of new outbound investment rules that take effect July 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: 新华社北京6月1日电 国务院总理李强日前签署国务院令，公布《国务院关于对外投资的规定》（以下简称《规定》），自2026年7月1日起施行... 《规定》共34条

key_facts.fact: The framework gives Beijing the legal basis to force unwinding of completed overseas transactions and applies to deals in markets beyond mainland China, including Taiwan; it also lets China retaliate against foreign firms whose home countries restrict Chinese investment.
key_facts.excerpt: The regulations, published by the State Council, or cabinet, seek to influence deals in markets beyond mainland China, including Taiwan, and give Beijing the power to punish foreign firms whose home countries restrict Chinese investment. The framework, which takes effect July 1, provides a comprehensive and formalised legal basis for China to force the unwinding of completed overseas transactions

key_facts.fact: Investors are barred from transferring restricted goods, technology, services and related data abroad — including through cross-border deployment of technical staff, overseas training, or remote technical guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the regulation, effective July 1, investors are prohibited from transferring restricted goods, technology, services and data overseas. Companies are also banned from providing technical training in order to export those things

key_facts.fact: Violators face fines of up to 1% of the investment amount and may be ordered to halt transactions and dispose of assets.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors that undertake prohibited overseas investments may be ordered to halt transactions, dispose of assets and pay fines of up to 1 per cent of the investment amount.

key_facts.fact: The decree was adopted at the State Council's 83rd executive meeting on April 17, days before Beijing ordered Meta to unwind its $2 billion acquisition of agentic AI startup Manus.
key_facts.excerpt: The new rules were adopted at a meeting of the State Council on April 17, days before China ordered the cancellation of Meta Platforms' US$2 billion (S$2.5 billion) acquisition of agentic AI startup Manus.

key_facts.fact: Beijing can ban foreign entities from trading or investing in China and cancel work or entry visas of foreign employees if their home countries put Chinese firms on sanctions lists.
key_facts.excerpt: Monday's regulations also give Beijing the power to ban foreign entities from trading with or investing in China, and even cancel their foreign employees' China work or entry visas if their home countries restrict Chinese investment.

stories.headline: US and Iran trade strikes as Trump tightens terms on draft war-ending MOU

key_facts.fact: The US military said it struck Iranian military sites on Sunday-Monday and Iran's IRGC said it targeted a US base in response; Kuwait reported intercepting missiles and drones — day 94 of the US-Israel war on Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States military says it has struck Iranian military sites, and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it has targeted a US base in response, the latest in a series of exchanges as negotiations to end the three-month US-Israel war on Iran are conducted.

key_facts.fact: President Trump met with senior aides on Friday to make a 'final determination' on the framework but the meeting ended without a deal, and reports later said he requested fresh changes to the draft text.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump and senior aides met on Friday to make a 'final determination' about a framework for extending the ceasefire, but the meeting concluded without clarity on the next steps before reports later emerged that the president had requested changes to the text.

key_facts.fact: The latest draft includes a 60-day cessation of hostilities, a call to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and a framework to resume negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme, per CBS News reporting cited by other outlets.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest terms includes a 60-day cessation of violence and a call to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, CBS News reported - the shipping lane through which approximately one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments usually pass... It also reportedly includes a framework to reopen negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme

key_facts.fact: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said no negotiations had taken place on the nuclear file and that ending the war was Tehran's priority; an end to the Lebanon conflict remained 'an essential condition' for any deal.
key_facts.excerpt: 'No negotiations have taken place on the details of the nuclear file. At this stage, our priority is ending the war,' Baghaei told a press briefing. He added that an end to the conflict in Lebanon remained an 'essential condition' for any deal

key_facts.fact: Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned on state TV that the United States 'was not to be trusted' and that Tehran would not approve any agreement 'until we are certain that the rights of the Iranian people have been upheld'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's chief negotiator warned on Sunday the United States was not to be trusted, saying Tehran would not agree to any deal with Washington unless it fully secured Iranian rights... 'We will not approve any agreement until we are certain that the rights of the Iranian people have been upheld,' Ghalibaf said in a video broadcast on state television.

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social that 'Iran really wants to make a deal, and it will be a good one for the U.S.A. and those that are with us', adding he was in 'no hurry' to finalize a pact.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Iran really wants to make a deal, and it will be a good one for the U.S.A. and those that are with us,' Trump said in a Truth Social post.

key_facts.fact: Negotiations have run primarily through Pakistani and Qatari mediators rather than direct talks, and it is unclear what role Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — who has not been seen in public since his succession on March 8 — plays in finalizing the MOU.
key_facts.excerpt: the negotiations have taken place primarily through Pakistani and Qatari mediators, rather than direct U.S.-Iran talks, it has never been clear whether the two sides have been working on the same version of the MOU... Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, son of the leader slain in the opening U.S.-Israeli salvo of the war, has not been seen in public since his succession on March 8.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Saratov refinery and Kirov pumping station; Russia accuses Kyiv of hitting Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed overnight strikes on the Rosneft Saratov oil refinery causing 'a large-scale fire', plus the Lazarevo oil pumping station in Russia's Kirov region — about 1,300 km (800 miles) from Ukrainian-held territory — that serves the Surgut-Gorky-Polotsk pipeline shipping Russian oil to Belarus.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's military confirmed that it ⁠had struck the Saratov oil refinery overnight... In the Kirov region, northeast of Moscow and about 1,300km (800 miles) from Ukraine, Governor Alexander Sokolov said ⁠drones had hit a ⁠facility in the Urzhumsky district. The Ukrainian army confirmed the attack, saying it had ⁠also ⁠hit the Lazarevo oil-pumping station in the region.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defence Ministry said it shot down 216 drones overnight; Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 229 Shahed, Gerbera and Italmas drones at Ukraine, of which 212 were downed and 14 hit their targets at 11 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: Not all the drones struck their ⁠targets. Russia's Defence Ministry said it had downed 216 drones overnight... Ukraine's air force said Russia had launched 229 drones overnight, 212 ⁠of which were downed over ‌northern and eastern Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Russia's state nuclear company Rosatom said a Ukrainian 'kamikaze combat drone' struck the turbine hall of Power Unit No. 6 at the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on Saturday, tearing a hole in the wall; CEO Alexei Likhachev called the attack 'deliberate' but said primary equipment was undamaged.
key_facts.excerpt: 'This afternoon, a Ukrainian kamikaze combat drone ​struck the turbine hall building of Power Unit No. ​6, ‌resulting in a subsequent detonation,' Rosatom chief Alexei Likhachev said in a statement, calling the incident 'deliberate.' 'The explosion caused no damage to the primary equipment; However, it ‌tore a hole in the turbine hall wall'

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's military denied attacking the Zaporizhzhia plant, calling it 'yet another propaganda ploy', and said it adheres to international humanitarian law.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's military said it did not target or strike the plant and described the Russian claim as 'yet another propaganda ploy.' A military statement said that it adheres to international humanitarian law and is aware of the 'consequences of any actions targeting nuclear facilities.'

key_facts.fact: IAEA head Rafael Grossi said 'attacking nuclear sites is like playing with fire' and the agency's team at the plant requested first-hand access to the affected turbine building; it would be the first drone attack within the plant's perimeter since April 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Attacking nuclear sites is like playing with fire,' it cited Grossi as saying and further added that an IAEA team at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has requested access to 'examine the affected turbine building first-hand.' The agency said it would be the first drone attack within the plant site's perimeter since April 2024.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine also confirmed strikes on a fuel depot in Matveyev Kurgan (Rostov region), drone command centers in Kalynove (Donetsk region) and Grafovka (Belgorod region), and a drone-assembly workshop in occupied Donetsk; three civilians were injured in Belgorod.
key_facts.excerpt: Beyond hitting the strategic Rosneft oil refinery in Saratov, Ukrainian forces struck a vital crude oil pumping station and a fuel depot. The operation also heavily targeted the Kremlin's frontline capabilities, neutralizing a Russian command and observation post, drone command centers, a UAV workshop, and troop concentrations.

stories.headline: FT: Iran's military increasingly weaponizes ChatGPT and Gemini for cyber operations

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported that Iran's military and cyber apparatus are increasingly using Western AI tools including OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini to support cyber operations, intelligence gathering and military research, citing cybersecurity researchers and Iranian officials.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's military and cyber apparatus are increasingly using artificial intelligence tools including ChatGPT and Gemini to support cyber operations, intelligence gathering and military research, according to a report by the Financial Times.

key_facts.fact: Iranian-linked actors have used AI systems to improve phishing campaigns, generate malicious code, create convincing online personas and identify vulnerabilities in target networks; researchers said AI has 'lowered the barriers' to cyber operations.
key_facts.excerpt: The report, citing cybersecurity researchers and Iranian officials, said Iranian-linked actors have used AI systems to improve phishing campaigns, generate malicious code, create convincing online personas and identify vulnerabilities in target networks. Researchers told the newspaper that artificial intelligence has lowered the barriers to conducting cyber operations

key_facts.fact: Iranian authorities are also pursuing broader military AI applications including drone technology, electronic warfare and battlefield decision-making systems.
key_facts.excerpt: The Financial Times said Iranian authorities have also promoted broader military applications of AI, including research into drone technology, electronic warfare and battlefield decision-making systems.

key_facts.fact: Check Point Research found that the IRGC-affiliated threat actor Nimbus Manticore (UNC1549) leveraged LLM-based tools and AI-assisted development to build new malware including 'MiniFast' during Operation Epic Fury after February 2026 kinetic strikes; Palo Alto Unit 42 tracked 7,381 phishing URLs across 1,881 domains tied to Iranian campaigns through April 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: In the recent campaign, the actor adopted several new techniques, including AppDomain (application domain) hijacking, AI-assisted malware development, and SEO poisoning... During Operation Epic Fury, we continued to observe activity from the threat actor. Despite the challenging environment, Nimbus Manticore demonstrated a strong ability to rapidly adapt, maintain infrastructure, and develop new tooling. We assess that this capability was likely supported, at least in part, by LLM-based tools and AI-assisted development techniques.

key_facts.fact: Google's Threat Intelligence Group documented in a February 2026 follow-up that Iran's APT42 used Gemini for reconnaissance and accelerating malware development, and identified HONESTCUE, a malware framework that outsources code generation to Gemini's API via reframed prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's APT42 used Gemini to search for official email addresses, conduct reconnaissance on potential business partners for phishing pretexts, and accelerate malware development and exploitation techniques. The February 2026 follow-up identified HONESTCUE, a malware framework that sends prompts via Gemini's API to outsource code generation, receiving C# source code as responses to function as a downloader and launcher.

stories.headline: Index providers rewrite eligibility rules to fast-track SpaceX into S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and Russell 1000

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is heading for a June 12, 2026 Nasdaq debut under the ticker SPCX, with a targeted raise of $75 billion-plus at a $1.5-$2 trillion valuation and an expected public float of only 3%-5%.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX (expected ticker: SPCX) is heading for a June 2026 Nasdaq debut at a $1.5T–$2T valuation, raising $75B+ in what may be the largest IPO in history... Expected public float 3% – 5% (~$45B – $100B tradable)

key_facts.fact: Nasdaq approved a fast-entry framework on March 30, 2026, effective May 1, that lets newly-public companies enter the Nasdaq-100 after 15 trading days if they rank within the top 40 holdings by size.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 30, 2026, Nasdaq approved its own fast-entry framework, with implementation scheduled for May 1, 2026. Morningstar reported that Nasdaq's model would permit newly public companies into indexes after 15 trading days if they ranked within the top 40 holdings by size.

key_facts.fact: FTSE Russell announced on May 26, 2026 a new fast-track framework letting qualifying large IPOs enter the Russell US Indexes and FTSE GEIS five trading days after listing — widely seen as a 'green lane' for SpaceX, whose investable market cap is projected at about $70 billion post-listing.
key_facts.excerpt: FTSE Russell announced on May 26 that it had completed revisions to its IPO fast-track framework. The new rules stipulate that qualifying large-scale IPOs will be formally included in relevant major indexes after the market close on the fifth trading day following their initial listing, dramatically shortening the previous timeline that required waiting for quarterly reviews. The change is widely viewed by markets as a bespoke 'green lane' tailored for SpaceX. According to FTSE Russell's assessment, SpaceX's investable market capitalization post-listing is expected to reach approximately $70 billion.

key_facts.fact: S&P Dow Jones opened a consultation in May 2026 proposing to cut the S&P 500 seasoning window from 12 months to 6 months for megacap IPOs and to waive the four-quarter GAAP profitability test above a market-cap threshold — reversing post-dot-com 'Core Earnings' reforms from 2002.
key_facts.excerpt: S&P Dow Jones Indices opened a consultation in May 2026 proposing to reduce the seasoning window from 12 months to 6 months for megacap IPOs and to waive the four-quarter GAAP profitability test when the issuer exceeds a market-cap threshold. The Investable Weight Factor (IWF) — which normally caps a low-float stock's effective weight at its actual float percentage — is also under review for relaxation.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX reported a Q1 2026 GAAP loss of $4.28 billion and a roughly $2.6 billion FY 2025 loss, making it the most unprofitable firm ever fast-tracked into blue-chip indexes; Starlink contributed $3.26 billion (69%) of Q1 revenue and was the sole profitable segment.
key_facts.excerpt: In the first quarter of this year, Starlink contributed $3.26 billion in revenue — lifting its share to 69% — and was the sole profitable segment, posting operating income of $1.19 billion.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX structured a phased insider lock-up letting insiders sell up to 20% of locked shares after the first quarterly earnings (covering through June), plus an additional 10% if the stock is trading 30% above the IPO price — a design that helps boost free float quickly to qualify for Nasdaq-100 fast entry.
key_facts.excerpt: After reporting earnings for the three months through June - the company's first results as a public company – insiders can sell up to 20% of their eligible locked-up shares. If this stock is also trading at least 30% above the IPO price at that point, they can sell an additional 10%... The unique lock-up structure is likely a response to new Nasdaq rules to include 'fast entry' for new listings to be included on the Nasdaq 100.

stories.headline: US Army's 'Operation Jailbreak' pushes hacked weapons-system patches to CENTCOM mid-sprint

key_facts.fact: Operation Jailbreak — a 30-day Army-industry sprint at Fort Carson, Colorado that began in early May and concludes June 6 — has involved hundreds of engineers from more than 50 defense companies trying to make legacy and new systems interoperable.
key_facts.excerpt: Operation Jailbreak was R2I's first volley and is nearing the end of its first month-long 'sprint.' Officials said hundreds of engineers and more than 50 defense companies have participated, despite the industry tradition of insularity.

key_facts.fact: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has called it 'the largest hackathon in human history' and Army CTO Alex Miller said updates from the first jailbroken systems — including command-and-control tying counter-UAS radars, cameras and effectors together — are already being pushed to US Central Command in the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We have already been pushing updates from here down to Central Command,' Alex Miller, the Army's chief technology officer, told reporters Thursday. 'One of the first couple systems that were jailbroken was really our command and control, our C2 platform, and the ability to actually tie in a lot of the counter-UAS, the counter unmanned system, radars, cameras, and effectors.'

key_facts.fact: The participating companies include Anduril, Boeing, General Dynamics, L3Harris, Leidos, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Palantir, Perennial Autonomy and RTX, working under a 'Right to Integrate' (R2I) framework that mandates open APIs.
key_facts.excerpt: Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll and leaders from Anduril, Boeing, General Dynamics, L3Harris, Leidos, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Palantir, Perennial Autonomy and RTX announced May 5 that they will 'sprint' to conduct a series of combined Army and defense industry partnered hackathon events to integrate critical military technology systems.

key_facts.fact: Driscoll said the initiative was inspired by Ukraine's Delta command operating system, which he saw during a Germany trip; the Iran war 'wrought an urgent need for integrated U.S. defenses against Tehran's deadly, one-way attack drones'.
key_facts.excerpt: R2I was also galvanized by the Iran War, which wrought an urgent need for integrated U.S. defenses against Tehran's deadly, one-way attack drones... Driscoll had a 'light bulb' moment for the 'hackathon' during a recent trip to Germany, where Ukrainians demonstrated the fruits of their efforts: the Delta system, which quickly pulls information from various battlefield sources into a common, real-time picture unlike the dissonant American configuration.

key_facts.fact: The hackathon also spurred the Department of Defense's first Application Programming Interface marketplace, where interfaces can be documented and shared for interoperability.
key_facts.excerpt: The hackathon also spurred an Application Programming Interface marketplace, the first of its kind in the Department of Defense where interfaces can be documented and shared for interoperability.
